summary:
Cluster C delivers the paper's centerpiece (item 5): at EVERY ordinary primitive canonical seed of period p>1, Kahn's canonical localization -- the dynamical localization of (i^p, f^p) at A=K_p with removal of B=\mathcal{K}_p, exactly as constructed in Kahn I (arXiv:math/0609045) -- has a noninjective localized inclusion \hat i: T'_A -> T_A. The mechanism is exact and fully constructive. The source marked surface removes F^{-1}B while the target removes only B; the degree budget (global degree 2^p versus central local degree 2, so excess 2^p-2>0) forces an excess component X != A of F^{-1}A that is disjoint from B. A peripheral based loop gamma around X has winding number 1 about any x in X, hence lies outside the source localization subgroup H_s (whose loops live in a Jordan neighborhood D_A missing X), yet gamma bounds across the isolating disk D_X inside the target complement, so (i^p)_*[gamma]=1 in H_t. This subgroup-reflection defect a_*^{-1}(H_t) \supsetneq H_s converts, via the covering endpoint criterion, into an actual identification of two distinct source-cover endpoints by the localized inclusion -- an explicit point collision with a complete certificate (excess component, itinerary, access, subgroups, sheets, target point). The defect is moreover infinite: the cosets gamma^n H_s are pairwise distinct, which is the "infinite sheet resolution" datum the paper's replacement carrier must retain. The collision propagates verbatim through Kahn's exact equalizer pullback iteration to every depth, with a recorded inverse-sheet word, in particular to the KL direct-decoration depths m = nu*q+1, n = (nu-1)*q+1, where it forces same-tile collisions of every compatible full universal-cover tile lift and noninjectivity of the full glued pseudo-piece inclusion.

Scope is governed by the section-8 realization quantifier and must be reproduced exactly: (1) the collision is unconditional at every ordinary primitively p-renormalizable quadratic polynomial, p>1; (2) propagation through every pullback depth of that same seed is unconditional; (3) noninjectivity of the exact direct-decoration maps I_{m,n}, their tile lifts, and their glued pseudo-piece inclusions is asserted only WHENEVER that same seed carries KL direct-decoration data -- no inference that an arbitrary abstract canonical seed has a particular decoration, and no source-locked parameter realization is used or claimed. The result is corrective and lives on the inclusion arrow only: it invalidates any argument that treats canonical localization as embedding-preserving (Kahn's source asserts immersion, never embedding) and shows the full embedded pseudo-piece cannot be the universal carrier invariant; it says nothing against KL's separate dynamical covering arrow and does not prove VAAPC-I, UPTCR, rigidity, or MLC. A companion script machine-checks only source-lock strings, the 2^p arithmetic for 2<=p<=64, and ledger routing -- no topology or analysis is machine-verified.

%% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Notation and standing conventions for the forced-collision cluster
%% (canonical localization at an ordinary primitive seed).
%% amsart; requires amsmath, amssymb, amsthm.  Equation tags mirror the
%% source research note kl_canonical_localization_forced_collision.md
%% for traceability.
%% ---------------------------------------------------------------------

%% Theorem environments (omit any already declared in the preamble).
\theoremstyle{plain}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
\newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{definition}[theorem]{Definition}
\newtheorem{remark}[theorem]{Remark}

\subsection*{Standing conventions}

\begin{itemize}
\item A \emph{full continuum} is a nonempty compact connected set \(K\subset\mathbb C\) whose complement \(\mathbb C\setminus K\) is connected.  We write \(K\Subset U\) for compact containment.
\item \(f\colon U^1\to U^0\) is an \emph{ordinary} quadratic-like restriction of a quadratic polynomial, primitively renormalizable of period \(p>1\).  We set \(U^r=f^{-r}(U^0)\); then \(U^{r+1}\subset U^r\) and every restriction \(f\colon U^{r+1}\to U^r\) is quadratic-like (Kahn, arXiv:math/0609045, \texttt{pullback.tex}, ll.~2--7).
\item \(F=f^p\colon U^p\to U^0\), a proper holomorphic map of degree \(2^p\); \(i^p\colon U^p\hookrightarrow U^0\) is the \emph{physical inclusion}.
\item \(K_p\) is the filled Julia set of the \(p\)-renormalization; \(K_p(j)=f^j(K_p)\) for \(0\le j<p\); \(\mathcal K_p=\bigcup_{j=0}^{p-1}K_p(j)\).  Primitivity means the \(K_p(j)\) are pairwise disjoint (\texttt{intro.tex}, ll.~22--44).
\item \(A=K_p\), \(B=\mathcal K_p\).  The marked source and target surfaces of the canonical localization are
\[
 T'=(U^p\setminus F^{-1}B)\cup A,
 \qquad
 T=(U^0\setminus B)\cup A,                     \tag{1.1}
\]
and \(a=i^p\colon T'\to T\) is the restriction of the physical inclusion.  For the physical inclusion \(A'=(i^p)^{-1}(A)=A\): the marked continuum is literally the same set on both sides.
\item \(\Omega_s=T'\setminus A=U^p\setminus F^{-1}B\) and \(\Omega_t=T\setminus A=U^0\setminus B\).
\item \(D_A\Subset T'\) is a fixed Jordan local neighborhood of \(A\), disjoint from every other component of \(F^{-1}B\); \(z_*\in D_A\setminus A\) is the localization basepoint.  The \emph{localization subgroups} are
\[
 H_s=\operatorname{im}\bigl[\pi_1(D_A\setminus A,z_*)\longrightarrow\pi_1(\Omega_s,z_*)\bigr],  \tag{5.2}
\]
and \(H_t\le\pi_1(\Omega_t,a(z_*))\), defined analogously from a Jordan local neighborhood of \(A\) in \(T\); these are the subgroups to which Kahn's connected-complement localization covers correspond (\texttt{psiql2.tex}, ll.~434--505).
\item \(\pi_s\colon\widehat\Omega_s\to\Omega_s\), \(\pi_t\colon\widehat\Omega_t\to\Omega_t\) are the localization covers; \(\widehat a\colon\widehat\Omega_s\to\widehat\Omega_t\) is the unique commuting lift of \(a\); \(\widehat i\colon T'_A\to T_A\) is Kahn's localized inclusion between the completed localized marked surfaces.
\item For \(x\in\mathbb C\setminus\Omega_s\) (in practice \(x\in X\subset F^{-1}B\)), \(\operatorname{Ind}_x\colon\pi_1(\Omega_s,z_*)\to\mathbb Z\) is the winding-number homomorphism about \(x\).
\item \emph{Pullback dynasty:} \((i_r,f_r)\colon(\mathbf U^{r+1},K^{r+1})\to(\mathbf U^r,K^r)\), \(r\ge0\), is Kahn's exact pullback iteration of the canonical seed \((i_0,f_0)=(\widehat i,\widehat f)\), realized by the equalizers
\[
 \mathbf U^{r+2}=\{(x,y):i_r(x)=f_r(y)\},
 \quad i_{r+1}(x,y)=y,\quad f_{r+1}(x,y)=x     \tag{2.1}
\]
(\texttt{psiql2.tex}, ll.~350--416).  \(A_r=\mathbf U^r\setminus K^r\) is the complementary annulus at depth \(r\).  For \(m>n\ge0\),
\(I_{m,n}=i_n\circ i_{n+1}\circ\cdots\circ i_{m-1}\colon A_m\to A_n\).
\item \emph{KL direct-decoration data:} \(P=Y^{(\nu-1)q+1}\) with the two univalent \(f^q\)-pullbacks \(Q_L,Q_R\subset P\) of depth \(\nu q+1\) (KL~II, \texttt{kingdom.tex}, ll.~116--155).  The \emph{exact direct-decoration depths} are \(m=\nu q+1\) and \(n=(\nu-1)q+1\).
\item \emph{Tile conventions:} \(T_s\), \(T_t\) generate the deck groups of the universal covers of the source and target annuli; a \emph{compatible universal-cover tile lift} \(L\) of \(I_{m,n}\) is a lift to those universal covers satisfying the degree-one equivariance \(L\circ T_s=T_t\circ L\).  KL's pseudo-pieces are glued from universal-cover tiles of complementary components, and each source tile is embedded in its source pseudo-piece (KL~II, \texttt{psiql.tex}, ll.~169--207).
\end{itemize}

theorems.name: Jordan-neighborhood basis
theorems.label: lem:jordan-basis
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source document (its Lemma 3.1); transcription expands the compactness step choosing r close to 1, with no new claims.

theorems.name: One quadratic pullback
theorems.label: lem:quadratic-pullback
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
Choose the nested Jordan basis \(V_r\) of Lemma \ref{lem:jordan-basis}, with each \(\partial V_r\) avoiding \(v\); if \(v\notin K\), choose \(\overline V_1\) disjoint from \(v\).

\emph{Case \(v\notin K\).}  Then \(v\notin V_r\) for every \(r\), so
\(q\colon q^{-1}(V_r)\to V_r\)
is an unbranched proper covering of total degree two.  Since \(V_r\) is simply connected, its preimage has exactly two components \(W_r^0,W_r^1\), and each restriction \(q\colon W_r^k\to V_r\) is a biholomorphism.  The two inverse branches of \(q\) on \(V_1\) label the components coherently for all \(r\), and the nesting \(\overline V_{r+1}\subset V_r\) gives
\[
 \overline W_{r+1}^k\subset W_r^k,\qquad k=0,1.
\]
Set \(L_k=\bigcap_{r\ge1}\overline W_r^k\).  As a nested intersection of nonempty compact connected sets, each \(L_k\) is nonempty, compact, and connected.  It is full because
\[
 \mathbb C\setminus L_k=\bigcup_{r\ge1}\bigl(\mathbb C\setminus\overline W_r^k\bigr)
\]
is an increasing union of connected sets: each \(\overline W_r^k\) is a closed Jordan disk, since \(\partial V_r\) avoids the critical value and the inverse branch carries \(V_r\) and its regular boundary biholomorphically.  The inverse branches identify each \(L_k\) homeomorphically with \(K=\bigcap_r\overline V_r\), and \(q^{-1}K=L_0\sqcup L_1\).

\emph{Case \(v\in K\).}  Every \(V_r\) contains \(v\).  The component \(W_r\) of \(q^{-1}(V_r)\) containing the critical point \(c\) maps with degree at least two; since the total degree is two, its degree is exactly two and \(W_r\) exhausts \(q^{-1}(V_r)\).  Riemann--Hurwitz for the proper degree-two map \(W_r\to V_r\) with its single simple critical point gives
\[
 \chi(W_r)=2\chi(V_r)-1=1,
\]
so \(W_r\) is a disk.  Because \(\partial V_r\) contains no critical value, \(\partial W_r\) is a regular Jordan curve.  The compact Jordan disks \(\overline W_r\) are nested, and
\[
 q^{-1}K=\bigcap_{r\ge1}\overline W_r.
\]
The same increasing-complement argument as in the first case shows that this intersection is connected and full.

For completeness, the bordered Riemann--Hurwitz step can be obtained by doubling \(W_r\) and \(V_r\) across their regular boundaries.  The doubled degree-two map of closed surfaces has exactly the critical point and its mirror, so
\[
 2-2g=2\cdot2-2=2,
\]
whence \(g=0\); and since the double of a planar domain with \(b\) boundary components has genus \(b-1\), we get \(b=1\), i.e.\ \(W_r\) is a disk with Jordan boundary.
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source document (its Lemma 3.2), including the doubling justification of bordered Riemann--Hurwitz.  The source's audit stresses this lemma exists precisely because a bare degree count is not a component theorem.

theorems.name: Connectivity after finitely many full deletions
theorems.label: lem:connectivity
theorems.statement_latex:
\begin{lemma}[Connectivity after finitely many full deletions]\label{lem:connectivity}
Let \(U\) be a plane topological disk and let \(C_1,\dots,C_N\Subset U\) be pairwise disjoint full continua.  Then
\[
 U\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N C_i
\]
is path connected.
\end{lemma}
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
Applying Lemma \ref{lem:jordan-basis} twice inside the disjoint neighborhoods used in Corollary \ref{cor:isolating-disks}, choose pairwise-disjoint Jordan domains
\[
 C_i\subset D_i^-,\qquad \overline{D_i^-}\subset D_i^+,\qquad \overline{D_i^+}\subset U.
\]
The finitely connected plane domain \(U_0=U\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N\overline{D_i^-}\) is connected: after a homeomorphism \(U\cong\mathbb D\), removing finitely many pairwise-disjoint closed Jordan disks compactly contained in \(\mathbb D\) leaves a disk with finitely many holes.  As an open connected subset of the plane, \(U_0\) is path connected.

For each \(i\), the open set \(D_i^+\setminus C_i\) is connected.  Indeed \(\mathbb C\setminus C_i\) is connected by fullness, and its intersection with the Jordan disk \(D_i^+\) cannot have a component separated from the outer collar of \(\partial D_i^+\): such a component would be a bounded complementary component of \(C_i\), contradicting fullness.  Hence \(D_i^+\setminus C_i\) is path connected.  It contains the nonempty annulus \(D_i^+\setminus\overline{D_i^-}\), which is also contained in \(U_0\); thus every \(D_i^+\setminus C_i\) has nonempty connected overlap with \(U_0\).  Their union is path connected and equals
\[
 U_0\cup\bigcup_{i=1}^N\bigl(D_i^+\setminus C_i\bigr)=U\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N C_i. \qedhere
\]
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source (its Lemma 3.5).

theorems.name: Excess central pullback (existence and position of X)
theorems.label: prop:excess
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
The global map \(F=f^p\colon U^p\to U^0\) is proper of degree \(2^p\) (Kahn, \texttt{pullback.tex}, ll.~2--7).  By the definition of the primitive quadratic-like renormalization, the central component \(A\) has local degree two under \(F\) (\texttt{psiql2.tex}, ll.~549--558).

Choose a sufficiently small Jordan neighborhood \(V\) of \(A\) inside the range of the quadratic-like renormalization.  The central component of \(F^{-1}(V)\) maps onto \(V\) with degree two.  The degrees of all components of \(F^{-1}(V)\) sum to \(2^p\), and since \(p>1\),
\[
 2^p-2>0,
\]
so there is a component \(W\) of \(F^{-1}(V)\) other than the central one.  The proper map \(F\colon W\to V\) is onto, so \(W\) contains a point of \(F^{-1}(A)\).  The component \(X\) of \(F^{-1}(A)\) through that point lies in \(W\), hence is not the central component \(A\).  This proves (4.1).

For \(0\le j<p\) write \(K_j=K_p(j)=f^j(A)\).  Since \(F=f^p\) commutes with \(f^j\) on these sets and \(F(A)=A\),
\[
 F(K_j)=f^j(F(A))=f^j(A)=K_j.                       \tag{4.3}
\]
Suppose \(X\cap K_j\ne\varnothing\).  If \(j\ne0\), a point of the intersection is mapped by \(F\) into both \(A\) (because \(X\subset F^{-1}A\)) and \(K_j\) (by (4.3) and invariance), contradicting the primitive disjointness \(A\cap K_j=\varnothing\).  If \(j=0\), then \(X\cap A\ne\varnothing\), so the two connected subsets \(X\) and \(A\) of \(F^{-1}A\) lie in one component, forcing \(X=A\), again a contradiction.  Hence (4.2).
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source (its Proposition 4.1 plus the component-certificate paragraph).  The audit explicitly rejects the shortcut 'global degree 2^p is a component theorem' -- Lemmas 3.1--3.2 supply the missing finiteness/fullness.  The 2^p-2>0 arithmetic is (trivially) machine-checked for 2 <= p <= 64 in the companion script; the topology is not machine-checked.

theorems.name: Localization subgroup defect (winding-number calculation)
theorems.label: thm:subgroup-defect
theorems.statement_latex:
\begin{theorem}[Localization subgroup defect]\label{thm:subgroup-defect}
Let \(X\) and \(D_X\) be as in Proposition \ref{prop:excess} and (4.5), and let \(H_s\), \(H_t\) be the localization subgroups of (5.2).  Let \(\eta\subset\Omega_s\) be any path from \(z_*\) to \(\partial D_X\) and set
\[
 \gamma=\eta\cdot\partial D_X\cdot\overline\eta.       \tag{5.3}
\]
Then
\[
 [\gamma]\notin H_s,\qquad a_*[\gamma]=1\in H_t,
\]
and consequently
\[
 a_*^{-1}(H_t)\supsetneq H_s:                          \tag{5.7}
\]
the exact failure of the subgroup-reflection equality on the actual canonical-localization data.
\end{theorem}
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
First, \(a=i^p\) maps \(\Omega_s\) into \(\Omega_t\): if \(z\in B\), then \(z\in K_j\) for some \(j\), so \(F(z)\in F(K_j)=K_j\subset B\) by (4.3); hence \(B\subset F^{-1}B\), and therefore \(U^p\setminus F^{-1}B\subset U^0\setminus B\).

The removed family \(F^{-1}B\) is a finite union of pairwise disjoint full continua by Corollary \ref{cor:finite-pullback}, so \(\Omega_s=U^p\setminus F^{-1}B\) is path connected by Lemma \ref{lem:connectivity}; the path \(\eta\) exists, and \(\gamma\) of (5.3) is a well-defined based loop at \(z_*\).

Fix \(x\in X\).  Winding number about \(x\) defines a homomorphism \(\operatorname{Ind}_x\) on \(\pi_1(\Omega_s,z_*)\), since \(x\in X\subset F^{-1}B\) is disjoint from \(\Omega_s\).  Every element of \(H_s\) is represented, before inclusion, by a loop in \(D_A\setminus A\); the Jordan disk \(D_A\) is disjoint from every component of \(F^{-1}B\) other than \(A\), so \(x\notin D_A\), and any loop inside the simply connected \(D_A\) is null-homotopic in \(\mathbb C\setminus\{x\}\).  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Ind}_x(H_s)=\{0\}.                     \tag{5.4}
\]
On the other hand, the path and reverse path in (5.3) cancel in winding number, while \(\partial D_X\) (positively oriented) has winding number one about \(x\in X\subset D_X\).  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{Ind}_x(\gamma)=1,\qquad [\gamma]\notin H_s.  \tag{5.5}
\]
For the target: (4.5) gives \(\overline D_X\cap B=\varnothing\), and \(D_X\subset U^p\subset U^0\); hence \(D_X\subset\Omega_t\), and \(\partial D_X\) contracts across the disk \(D_X\) inside \(\Omega_t\).  Therefore
\[
 a_*[\gamma]=1\in H_t.                                \tag{5.6}
\]
Combining (5.5) and (5.6), \([\gamma]\in a_*^{-1}(H_t)\setminus H_s\), which is (5.7).
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source (its Section 5).  The audit notes: the loop is based (unbased-loop shortcut avoided; conjugation by eta does not change winding), and winding/homology is used only for the negative statement [gamma] not in H_s -- the collision itself uses the exact covering endpoint criterion, not homology.  Basepoint conventions for H_t (transport along a) are supplied by the paper's notation; the source defines H_t 'analogously'.

theorems.name: Forced-collision theorem (main)
theorems.label: thm:forced-collision
theorems.caveats: This is the centerpiece; full proof in the source (its Sections 1, 5, 6).  It is a collision in Kahn's actual canonical-localization construction at an ordinary primitive polynomial stage, not an abstract-annulus or abstract psi-ql counterexample.  It concerns the inclusion arrow only (Kahn's localized i-leg, asserted in the source TeX to be an immersion, never an embedding); it makes no claim against the dynamical covering arrow.  It does NOT prove VAAPC-I, UPTCR, rigidity, or MLC.

theorems.name: Infinite coset defect (infinite sheet resolution datum)
theorems.label: prop:infinite-defect
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
Winding about \(x\in X\) gives a homomorphism \(w=\operatorname{Ind}_x\colon\pi_1(\Omega_s,z_*)\to\mathbb Z\) with
\[
 w(H_s)=\{0\},\qquad w(\gamma)=1,
\]
by (5.4)--(5.5).  Since \(a_*[\gamma]=1\) by (5.6), every power \(\gamma^n\) lies in \(a_*^{-1}(H_t)\).  If \(\gamma^nH_s=\gamma^mH_s\), then \(\gamma^{n-m}\in H_s\), so \(n-m=w(\gamma^{n-m})=0\).  Hence the cosets are pairwise distinct, and the pointed coset set is infinite.
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Full proof in the source (its Section 9).  The coset object is a pointed set, not a group, unless normality of H_s is separately proved -- the source states this caveat explicitly and the paper must keep it.  The follow-up interior-carrier factorization (KL_LOCALIZATION_SHEET_RESOLUTION_FACTORIZATION: unique factorization of the localized lift through the H_s-to-K covering with K=a_*^{-1}(H_t), embedded second leg, kernel pair carried by the covering leg) is cited by the source note as a separate theorem; its filled completion, selected direct-decoration component alignment, and prime-end realization are explicitly open.

theorems.name: Exact propagation through Kahn's pullback iteration and KL direct-decoration depths
theorems.label: thm:propagation
theorems.statement_latex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact propagation]\label{thm:propagation}
Let \((i_r,f_r)\colon(\mathbf U^{r+1},K^{r+1})\to(\mathbf U^r,K^r)\), \(r\ge0\), be Kahn's pullback iteration of the canonical seed \((i_0,f_0)=(\widehat i,\widehat f)\), realized by the exact equalizers (2.1), and put \(A_r=\mathbf U^r\setminus K^r\).  Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every \(r\ge0\) there are points \(x_r^+\ne x_r^-\in A_{r+1}\) with \(i_r(x_r^+)=i_r(x_r^-)=v_r\in A_r\); the choices made are recorded by a complete inverse-sheet word \(\omega=(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_1,\dots)\) appended to the certificate (6.3).
\item For all \(m>n\ge0\) the composed inclusion
\[
 I_{m,n}=i_n\circ i_{n+1}\circ\cdots\circ i_{m-1}\colon A_m\to A_n   \tag{7.4}
\]
is noninjective:
\[
 I_{m,n}(u)=I_{m,n}(v),\qquad u\ne v.                 \tag{7.5}
\]
\item If the same canonical seed carries KL direct-decoration data \(P=Y^{(\nu-1)q+1}\), \(Q_L,Q_R\subset P\) of depth \(\nu q+1\), then (7.5) holds at the exact direct-decoration depths
\[
 m=\nu q+1,\qquad n=(\nu-1)q+1,
\]
the source and target depths used by \(Q_L,Q_R\subset P\) --- not at an unrelated pullback depth.
\item \(I_{m,n}\) has annular degree \(+1\), and every compatible universal-cover tile lift \(L\) of \(I_{m,n}\) satisfies
\[
 L\bigl(T_s^{-k}\widetilde v\bigr)=L(\widetilde u)     \tag{7.6}
\]
at two distinct source points, where \(\widetilde u,\widetilde v\) lift \(u,v\) and \(k\in\mathbb Z\) is the unique integer with \(L(\widetilde v)=T_t^kL(\widetilde u)\).  Since KL's construction embeds each source tile in its source pseudo-piece, (7.6) survives the source gluing: it is a same-tile collision of the full inclusion-induced pseudo-piece immersion, which is therefore noninjective.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
\emph{Base case.}  The collision (6.1)--(6.2) of Theorem \ref{thm:forced-collision} lives in the complementary annulus of the localized seed: it gives
\[
 x_0^+\ne x_0^-\in A_1,\qquad i_0(x_0^+)=i_0(x_0^-)=v_0\in A_0.  \tag{7.1}
\]
(The two distinct source-cover points map to one target-cover point, and \(v_0\) lies off the filled continuum because both source points do.)

\emph{Induction step.}  Suppose
\[
 x_r^+\ne x_r^-\in A_{r+1},\qquad i_r(x_r^+)=i_r(x_r^-)=v_r\in A_r.  \tag{7.2}
\]
The restriction \(f_r\colon A_{r+1}\to A_r\) is an unbranched surjective covering, because \(f_r^{-1}(K^r)=K^{r+1}\) and all branch values of \(f_r\) lie in \(K^r\).  Choose \(y_r\in A_{r+1}\) with \(f_r(y_r)=v_r\).  In the exact equalizer (2.1) put
\[
 x_{r+1}^{\pm}=(x_r^{\pm},y_r).
\]
These are genuine points of \(\mathbf U^{r+2}\) because \(i_r(x_r^{\pm})=v_r=f_r(y_r)\); they are distinct because their first coordinates differ; and
\[
 x_{r+1}^+\ne x_{r+1}^-,\qquad i_{r+1}(x_{r+1}^{\pm})=y_r=:v_{r+1}.  \tag{7.3}
\]
Moreover \(x_{r+1}^{\pm}\in A_{r+2}\), since \(K^{r+2}=i_{r+1}^{-1}(K^{r+1})\) and \(i_{r+1}(x_{r+1}^{\pm})=y_r\notin K^{r+1}\).  This proves item (1); the recorded choices of the \(y_r\) constitute the complete inverse-sheet word \(\omega\), so no unlabeled existence step is used.

\emph{Item (2).}  At \(r=m-1\), (7.3) provides two distinct points \(u=x_{m-1}^+\), \(v=x_{m-1}^-\) of \(A_m\) with the same \(i_{m-1}\)-image.  Applying the remaining factors \(i_n\circ\cdots\circ i_{m-2}\) to that common image yields (7.5).

\emph{Item (3).}  For KL's direct-decoration pair one substitutes the actual depths \(m=\nu q+1\) and \(n=(\nu-1)q+1\) (KL~II, \texttt{kingdom.tex}, ll.~116--155), so (7.5) holds at the exact source and target depths used by \(Q_L,Q_R\subset P\).

\emph{Item (4).}  The inclusion-induced map \(I_{m,n}\) has annular degree \(+1\).  Let \(L\) be a compatible universal-cover tile lift, with deck generators \(T_s,T_t\) and degree-one equivariance \(L\circ T_s=T_t\circ L\), and let \(\widetilde u,\widetilde v\) be lifts of \(u,v\) in the source tile.  Since \(L(\widetilde u)\) and \(L(\widetilde v)\) project to the equal points \(I_{m,n}(u)=I_{m,n}(v)\), there is a unique integer \(k\) with \(L(\widetilde v)=T_t^kL(\widetilde u)\).  Equivariance gives
\[
 L\bigl(T_s^{-k}\widetilde v\bigr)=T_t^{-k}L(\widetilde v)=L(\widetilde u),
\]
and \(T_s^{-k}\widetilde v\ne\widetilde u\) because these two points project to \(v\ne u\).  KL's construction embeds each source tile in its source pseudo-piece (KL~II, \texttt{psiql.tex}, ll.~169--207), so the identification (7.6) survives the source gluing: it is a same-tile collision of the full inclusion-induced pseudo-piece immersion.
\end{proof}
